Mean Girls is arguably one of the best movies of the 2000s, and it’s no surprise fans continue to support the film that launched a mini franchise with a sequel, a musical reboot released in 2024, and a Tony-nominated musical. The talented movie cast has gone on to do amazing things, which has kept them mostly apart until now. For the first time in a long time, Lindsay Lohan reunited with some of her Mean Girls cast on the set of her newest film, Return to You, and I’m not the only one obsessed with the photos.

Lohan, who famously played Cady Heron in the 2004 flick, has been filming an upcoming Netflix film alongside Mean Girls director Mark Waters. Last month, Waters revealed the film was filming at an iconic Mean Girls location, and now it seems they’ve tapped some of the cast to join them in this walk down memory lane. Waters once again took to his Instagram to share the photos of the mini reunion with Sharron Matthews, Stefanie Drummond, and Daniel DeSanto:

A post shared by Mark Waters (@mark_s_waters)

For those who might need a refresher, Waters also included photos of Matthews, Drummond, and DeSanto as their Mean Girls characters Joan (a teacher), Bethany (a fellow high school student), and Jason (Gretchen’s on-again, off-again boyfriend). It’s so heartwarming seeing them reunite, and I’m not the only one who thinks so. Fellow Mean Girls actor Jonathan Bennett, who played Aaron Samuels, was quick to comment on the post, writing:

As much as I would love to see the Freakier Friday actress reunite with “The Plastics” in another movie, I’m obsessed with the fact that Waters and Lohan, who is also producing the project, chose to include some of the iconic but lesser-known actors from the film. It also makes sense since Return to You is set to take place in the noughties, 2008 to be exact.

Lohan will play a lonely attorney who has been accidentally sent an emotional DVD from a dying woman addressed to the woman’s husband (played by Henry Golding). While it’s unclear what role the trio will play in the Netflix rom-com, the photos do give us some clues. DeSanto is definitely going to be a lawyer of some sort; whether that be a coworker or an enemy remains to be seen. Matthews can be seen in an office setting, which makes me think she could be a potential client. Drummond looks like she’s in a home, so maybe she plays a sister or mother of the dying woman.

Of course, all of this is purely speculation at this point. With production of the romance film just starting, it’s going to be a while before Return to You is available for those with a Netflix subscription, but that also means that there’s time for even more Mean Girls references and cameos to make an appearance in the film. Until then, fans can stream Mean Girls with an active Paramount+ subscription.

#3767. GTA 6 is the ‘most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history’ despite the fact it’s locked at 30FPS, even on PS5 Pro

Even a choppy frame rate can't stop the hype train.

It’s official, folks; Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most pre-ordered game of all time, and players who helped set that record can now start pre-loading it.

With over seven million pre-purchases and counting, GTA VI has been on track to become the most pre-ordered video game ever made for months. This morning, the official PlayStation account on X confirmed that GTA VI has finally reached that impressive milestone, formally dethroning Cyberpunk 2077, which held the title of “most pre-ordered game of all time” since its 2020 release.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history!Mark the occasion with a video showcasing why GTAVI plays best on PS5Get ready for launch on November 19 by clearing PS5 storage space and pre-loading today: https://t.co/wTPa5E4DJY pic.twitter.com/WTQvHQs9cI

In a truly happy twist of fate, this groundbreaking moment synced up almost perfectly with Rockstar Games announcing through their website that GTA VI is now up for pre-loading. Anyone who’s already purchased a digital copy can now start downloading it to their console or PC, so it’ll be ready to play as soon as it releases on November 19, 2026.

As great as this news is, it also comes with a caveat. In the same post where they confirmed players can pre-load the game, Rockstar also explained that GTA 6 is locked at 30fps, even on the PlayStation 5 Pro, to ensure roughly the same quality across platforms.

Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants.

While plenty of gamers will be upset that they won’t be able to experience Leonida and all its unhinged beauty at 60fps, Rockstar confirmed that PS5 Pro owners will get a pretty crisp cut of the game thanks to PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution and higher ray-tracing support. It’s a small victory, but it’s a victory nonetheless.

In other happy news, Xbox CEO Asha Shar announced that GTA VI will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both the Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One as part of a newly unveiled “ten-year strategic partnership” with Take-Two

Today marks the first step in our new 10-year strategic partnership with Take-Two. GTA VI, already the most pre-ordered game ever on Microsoft Store, will be playable on XBOX One through cloud gaming when it launches on November 19. https://t.co/WTtRs6plZx

As sad as some people are about the hard 30fps limit, it’s clear that the GTA hype storm isn’t going anywhere. So if you’re one of the millions who’ve already downloaded GTA VI, now’s the perfect time to get it onto your system.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

Intel's G3 Extreme is a mighty impressive chip, and easily the headline feature of Acer's Predator Atlas 8. If you're looking to get the best handheld Panther Lake chip right now, Acer has swooped in at pretty much the cheapest price point on the market.

And if that's all you want, the Atlas 8 has my blessing. It's a solid device that makes use of the chip and offers compromises in memory and storage capacity (in the American market) to bring that cost down. Not only that, but if you buy one right now, you get a heaping of goodies with it.

But if you don't need top-of-the-line specs to have a good time, the Atlas 8 instead becomes just one of many very, very solid, yet very, very expensive handhelds on offer in a time that has become worse and worse thanks to the memory crisis.

✅ You want the G3 Extreme but cheaper: The Atlas 8 undercuts both MSI and OneXPlayer in pricing for a G3 Extreme handheld.

❌ You play fighters or platformers primarily: The D-pad is mushy and lacks distinction, making it unsatisfying and a tad unruly.

The fact this is the cheapest way of getting Intel's G3 is both a boon for Acer and an indictment of the memory crisis. If you've gotta buy soon, this offers perhaps the best price-to-performance ratio above $1,000.

8-inch WUXGA 1920 x 1200 (120 Hz refresh rate and 500 nits peak brightness)

The memory capacity is around average (Though lower than the high-end G3 Extreme offerings from MSI and OneXPlayer), and the storage is below average for a high-end handheld if you buy it in America.

Though 512 GB of storage isn't awful in a device you only want for gaming, the G3 Extreme is strong enough to take on even beefy, big-budget games, so it's a shame that the Atlas 8 can't hold all that many at once.

You are getting a strong feature set even outside of that chip, though. For one, TMR Sticks make for not only more efficient battery usage, but snappy, responsive controls. And you get Hall effect triggers too.

In a handful of games, with upscaling on and off (35 W plugged in)

Performance is the name of the game for the Acer Predator Atlas 8, and boy, does it perform. Compared to the Z2 Extreme, I saw figures generally between 30% and 50% better, but it manages to double the fps in Metro Exodus.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

That performance bump is especially noticeable in games like Black Myth: Wukong, which are just below what I'd consider playable on Z2 Extreme and just about playable on the G3 Extreme. The G3 Extreme is the best gaming handheld chip right now, and the Atlas 8 getting less capacious memory than the MSI Claw 8 Ex AI+ CG3EM does not hold it back much in my testing. In fact, in some places, it even performs ever so slightly better.

Scores in major productivity suites and benchmarking tools (35 W plugged in)

At 860 grams, the Atlas 8 is a bit on the heavy side. It's balanced well, not feeling particularly heavy on either side, but you do notice that weight after long gaming sessions. I'm fond of the textured grips, but I do feel spoiled by the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 I used prior, thanks to its great feel and small cutaway between the screen and the grips.

However, I would simply pick a different handheld if you are planning on playing a heavy amount of fighting games or platformers, as the D-Pad is mushy, making it not only lacking in accuracy but generally unsatisfying to use. It's hard to make out when you actually hit buttons on the D-Pad, and it has very little distinction between different directions, making corner hits quite awkward. In Animal Well, I swapped to the thumbstick and never looked back.

The triggers and bumpers are solid, though, and the macro buttons on the back are satisfying to hit. You can even use a toggle just under the triggers to swap them from micro switches to full travel. That's an on-the-fly level of customisation that's admirable at best, and unnoticeable at worst.

Everything else about the Acer Predator Atlas 8 feels high quality in terms of feel. It's sturdy, with buttons placed well, and they're satisfyingly clacky without being too loud. The sound on the triggers is too hollow for my liking, but they feel smooth to the touch and are plenty responsive.

Speaking of loud, the speakers built into the Atlas 8 can really thump. They are in the bottom left and bottom right of the device, near the screen, making them quite immersive in use. They're not the highest quality, with the clashing of steel sounding more tinny than I'd usually ask for, but they're certainly not bad given their size.

With fans set to auto and performance mode at the 35 W Turbo mode, the fans are noticeable (once again, I have been spoiled by the X20), especially in intensive games like Phantom Blade Zero. But they're not so loud that they would put me off using this handheld in its high-wattage mode. I measured the fans to be around 40 decibels at their peak (around a whisper), with it averaging 28-35 decibels in intensive games. Whilst benchmarking, that went up to the 50-decibel mark, though only very briefly.

Acer says it has equipped the Atlas 8 with a custom Predator AeroBlade cooling, and in practice, it's certainly cooler than the likes of the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X and Lenovo Legion G S (though it doesn't beat the X20).

It certainly gets fairly hot internally, but with the fans pointing upwards, I never noticed any of that heat on my fingertips.

Recorded in HW Info whilst performing gaming benchmarks (35 W plugged in)

Windows on a handheld can still be awkward. The Atlas 8 comes built in with Xbox's handheld software, which is somewhat like Microsoft's attempt at Steam, but it's not totally smooth sailing in any direction (though it's more efficient than Windows). For instance, you can't get Intel drivers through the Acer Predator software built into the device as you might expect, so you still have to go through the Intel updater or search the internet, except with a touchscreen. And the Xbox mode still opens up Steam independently if you want to play a Steam game.

As well as this, the Atlas 8 has two dedicated buttons to open up Acer's software, the Acer Predator Sense, but it doesn't always work on the first try, and I haven't figured out exactly why this is yet. The button on the left-hand side opens up a quick bar-style version of the app to swap between performance modes, change resolution, etc. The button on the right-hand side opens the full-fat Predator Sense app, where you can get more granular with your customisation.

Though it's effectively the same setup as the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X, it's slower and more cumbersome. That seems to be the prevailing truth of pretty much any Windows-based handheld right now.

I notice next to no difference between the 25W Quiet Mode and 30W Balanced Mode, with mere minutes being between them in the PC Mark 10 battery life gaming test.

However, Panther Lake's battery-saving mode (thanks to what Intel calls Endurance Gaming) is truly great, providing just under three hours of battery life. For less intensive use cases, I could see much better battery life. This Endurance mode can be flicked between three different modes, with one end bringing down power for better battery life, and the other bringing that power up in exchange for less battery life. The middle Balanced Mode is how I would use the handheld day-to-day.

The only downside here is that the very lightest mode on the Atlas 8 is currently 25 W, which is the max on Z2 Extreme handhelds while unplugged. You can push that down below 25 W, but you have to set a custom wattage, which I'd wager many handheld owners don't want to mess with. For most, you will be using this between 25 W and 35 W day-to-day.

Recorded using PCMark 10's gaming battery life test (Asus only goes up to 25 W unplugged but Acer goes up to 35 W)

Recorded using PCMark 10's gaming battery life test (Asus only goes up to 25 W unplugged but Acer goes up to 35 W)

Other than its fairly pretty face buttons, the Atlas 8 is a rather plain all-black gaming handheld. It goes without much intricate detailing (other than the Acer Predator RGB logo on the back and RGB rings around the thumbsticks).

As far as the display is concerned, you aren't getting any sort of fancy OLED here, but you do get a genuinely quite bright (500 nits) 16:10 WUXGA IPS display with Corning Gorilla Glass, making it decent in high-light environments. Importantly, I managed to play this out and about, and in front of a window, and could actually make out the game on screen, which is solid.

As of right now, it seems like the only model of the Atlas 8 with a G3 Extreme chip that sells in America comes with 512 GB of storage. That means you are getting half the storage and 75% of the memory of the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ CG3EM for 72% of the cost. But, as far as performance is concerned, I got pretty much identical stats, even beating out the Claw in 3DMark and losing in storage performance. That extra 8 GB of memory is unlikely to provide a major uplift in games, though the extra storage will certainly come in handy. My money would be on the Atlas 8 here.

Then, for the same price, one could pick up the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 (or the X for $300 less). Asus has the edge in ergonomics, look, thermals, screen, and storage capacity, but the G3 Extreme is a beast of a chip, handily handing Asus its butt in games. If you have got to pay upwards of $1,000 on a handheld right now, there's actually a good argument to be made for all three devices, though the Atlas 8 offers the best performance-to-price ratio.

It's a shame that Acer has to make little compromises to get that price down, but for $1,300, you will not get a better-performing gaming handheld in my book, and that's still quite impressive.

3. Best high performance: MSI Claw 8 EX AI+

👉Check out our full handheld gaming PC guide👈

The fact this is the cheapest way of getting Intel's G3 is both a boon for Acer and an indictment of the memory crisis. If you've gotta buy soon, this offers perhaps the best price-to-performance ratio above $1,000.

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

#3765. Nintendo's legendary Kirby designer Masahiro Sakurai weighs in on gen-AI, saying "it has yet to gain my trust" but not to reject it completely

"Doing nothing is probably not the right approach."

Masahiro Sakurai, the designer behind many iconic Nintendo franchises such as Super Smash Bros. and several Kirby titles, has weighed in on the ongoing discussion of generative-AI use in game development.

At an event celebrating the release of his new book - Masahiro Sakurai’s Thoughts on Games - the veteran director told Famitsu he hasn't and currently isn't using the technology to make games, noting that the role of a designer is to generate ideas.

"It has yet to gain my trust," Sakurai said via DeepL machine translation. Regarding graphical use specifically, he added that, "It must not amount to exploitation of any kind," and that "for the time being, we can produce better results by coming up with ideas ourselves".

But Sakurai is wary of rejecting gen-AI completely, saying "making games today is far too difficult", with some games "running at a loss even after selling millions of copies". A company in that position may go under if it does not change its stance on generative-AI, he suggested. "Doing nothing is probably not the right approach," he said, but "where and how to use it" is a complex topic with a lot of uncertainties. Sakurai is taking "a slow-paced approach" for now.

Outside of regular industry layoffs, the use of generative-AI in games has been the most controversial topic amongst developers and players. Some argue it's already being used in multiple development disciplines, notably programming and writing code. Others, such as Shigeru Miyamoto, are more sceptical of the technology's capabilities, especially when it comes to the more creative and art-driven parts of game development.

#3764. Activision cracking down on popular Call of Duty: Warzone app that basically constituted cheating

"Lobby shopping" is what Call of Duty: Warzone players have been calling the ability to check the skill level of players in a lobby prior to joining it, enabling them to pass on those that include a lot of tough competition.

There are several ways players, notably Twitch streamers and content creators, have been able to do that over the years. But the use of one app in particular - Warzone Agent - has been considered by many to be cheating, and Activision is finally doing something about it.

Alongside the launch of Modern Warfare 4's version of Warzone and the game's first season of post-launch content, Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet has announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"Yesterday, we began taking action against Warzone Agent, a paid, unauthorised third party tool that lets users lobby shop in Warzone," the developer revealed in a post on X. "Ricochet anti-cheat will block players attempting to load the software and instruct them to unload it before accessing multiplayer."

Having the ability to cherrypick the lobby with the lowest-skilled players possible bypasses the game's matchmaking algorithm, potentially ruining the game for the dozens of other players in the match. Historically, content creators have used the app (and other methods) to post impressive kill records.

The developer added in a follow-up message that: "Using unauthorised software to manipulate the player experience violates Activision terms of use and leaves your account and hardware subject to enforcement." The language seems to stop just short of outright confirming those players using Warzone Agent will be banned.

As part of this crackdown, Ricochet reiterated its stance on boosting - artificially increasing (or decreasing) one's skill rating - saying that it too is considered cheating. "Receiving a boost, having another player log in to boost your account, or purchasing a boosted account are all against policy," the developer said.

"Boosting services flood lobbies with low effort accounts used to farm XP and complete challenges. Those accounts can later be sold as Ranked Play ready, directly feeding the cheating marketplace."

More than 20,000 boosting-related accounts have been removed since the launch of Modern Warfare 4, according to the developer, and Ricochet will "continue to apply pressure" in this area.

The quality of multiplayer was a particular highlight in Eurogamer's review of Modern Warfare 4, in which Dom Peppiatt lauded the complexity of weapon handling, which works without taking away from accessibility of the gunplay.

Robert Downey Jr. has a habit of stealing the spotlight, and apparently, he has also stolen a Marvel Cinematic Universe record from one of his oldest co-stars. With Avengers: Doomsday hitting the 2026 movie calendar and bringing the former Iron Man actor back as Doctor Doom, Paul Bettany has lost something he briefly had all to himself. Judging by his reaction, he's taking it about as well as you'd expect from the man who used to live inside Tony Stark's computers.

Bettany, who is back playing Vision in the series VisionQuest, streaming with a Disney+ subscription, was recently asked about Downey's return during an interview with BBC Radio 1's Ali Plumb, who posted a clip of his interview to his Instagram. The actor pointed out that after Downey's exit in Avengers: Endgame, he could claim to be the MCU's longest-serving performer. Then Marvel decided to bring back his old boss. As Bettany joked in the video below, he said his former Avengers pal was stealing his “legacy.”

I love that he's treating this like yet another indignity Tony Stark has inflicted on him. Honestly, if you've spent nearly two decades working within the MCU, you deserve at least a little time to enjoy being the franchise's longest-serving employee. Unfortunately, Downey has apparently returned to collect his old parking space, too. As he hilariously put it:

He stole my legacy, as he has stolen so many other things from me. Maybe I still outlast him. We'll see.

The funny thing is that Bettany was there from the beginning. When 2008's Iron Man kicked off the MCU, the British actor voiced J.A.R.V.I.S., the artificially intelligent assistant helping Tony build suits, monitor threats and occasionally deliver a perfectly timed sarcastic comment. He didn't even have to show his face to become one of the franchise's most familiar performers.

Then, in 2015, Avengers: Age of Ultron gave him an actual body as Vision. Since then, Bettany has played the synthezoid across several Marvel movies as well as the TV show WandaVision and its aforementioned spinoff series, VisionQuest. That's an impressive career for someone who originally signed up to record a disembodied computer voice.

Downey, of course, was also there in 2008. He headlined Iron Man and helped turn Marvel into a box-office juggernaut before Tony's death in 2019's Endgame. Bettany kept appearing in new MCU projects after that, which gave him a brief moment atop the seniority chart. But with Downey officially playing Victor von Doom in December's Doomsday, the two actors will once again share a franchise history stretching back to the same first movie. So I wouldn't exactly call this a formal record being smashed. It's Bettany's wonderfully petty description of losing an exclusive bragging right.

And I hope their friendly rivalry continues. Bettany has previously spoken about how meaningful Vision has become to fans, especially those who identify with the character's struggle to belong. The actor's own MCU future remains open after VisionQuest, and he hasn't been officially confirmed for Doomsday. So, for the moment, his next opportunity to outlast Downey is still anybody's guess.

As for Downey, I'm curious to see how Marvel handles the actor who helped establish its cinematic universe now playing one of its most dangerous villains. Doomsday arrives on December 18 as part of the slate of upcoming new superhero movies, with Avengers: Secret Wars scheduled for the 2027 release calendar.

I'm rooting for Bettany to reclaim his title eventually, if only because I want to hear how he delivers the news. After all these years as J.A.R.V.I.S. and Vision, surely the man deserves to win one argument with Tony Stark.

#3762. Rockstar's doing a GTA 6 launch 'festival' in Miami featuring a lot of presumably expensive musical stars

The next-level glamour of Grand Theft Auto 6's arrival continues with word that Rockstar is hosting a star-studded launch 'festival' for the game in Miami - the game's setting-by-a-different-name.

The event will feature two stages hosting live performances by musical artists both featured in the game and from those who are not. Cardi B is probably the headliner - my knowledge of popular music is creaking here - but there's also Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Sofaygo, Ca7riel, and Paco Amoroso.

#3761. Overwatch doesn’t have ‘any intention’ of making 6-vs-6 the main mode, but it’s now ‘a second among equals’

The never-ending battle between Overwatch players choosing five-vs-five or six-vs-six will rage on.

In a new Director’s Take blog today, game director Aaron Keller confirmed that Overwatch will continue to support both formats, but with a renewed focus on the classic six-vs-six, which the studio is “starting to think of it as a second among equals.”

“We always say that we want to make the game you all want to play and it’s obvious that we have folks who want different things,” Keller said, citing player surveys that were very split between the two options, as seen above. “Over the past few years, we’ve realized that there doesn’t have to be a ‘winner’ between five-vs-five and six-vs-six. The real competition should be in your matches, not between two modes that can coexist. You can play either one (many people actually play both!) and we’re going to support that choice.”

Personally? I’m a fan of six-vs-six, but that’s because I’m a tank main. Solo tanking is a pain compared to having a buddy on the frontline with you, and I can see that there are many who agree with me…but also many who don’t. Overwatch will continue to feature both, Keller says, and there won’t be any radical switches soon either, other than an additional six-vs-six queue.

“Six-vs-six has been slowly growing in popularity over the last few years; however, the five-vs-five version of Open Queue was popular too,” Keller said. “We’d like to learn how many people are playing Open Queue six-vs-six for the role flexibility and how many people are playing it for the team size. Running both modes at the same time should produce some good data points to show us where we ought to be putting more energy.”

Keller warned that adding the new queue (Role Queue six-vs-six) instead of replacing an old one may impact queue times, but it “should be better overall for our community.” He also said that the team theorizes that some matchmaking changes coming in season six “will keep queue times more manageable” alongside the new option.

“We’ll put more energy into balance patches for [six-vs-six] and we’ll continue to look for the right format that really gives our community the experience they’re looking for,” Keller said. “Whether that’s Open Queue, Role Queue, a combination of both, or a new format that we’ve yet to try out, we’re here to figure out what works best for you.”

#3760. Nintendo Shuts Down Switch 2 Jailbreak, Sending Hackers Back To Square One

On October 22, news broke that the Switch 2 had been jailbroken for the first time. This meant that it wasâkindaâpossible to mod and dump games on the machine, which in the past would have opened the floodgates to third-party operating systems being installed and an accessible piracy scene. But not this time. Due to the incredibly complicated nature of the jailbreak, the need for now-delisted sofrware SmileBASIC, and that it was software based rather than hardware, Nintendo has been able to shut it down with its latest firmware update.

In the past, Nintendo’s portable consoles have become enormously popular among homebrew developers and the piracy scene for the ease with which they could be adapted. The Nintendo DS (its most successful console until the Switch, selling 154 million units and just shy of a billion games) had the infamous R4 cart onto which ROMs could be installed, while the original model of the Nintendo Switch (157 million units, 1.6 billion games) could be jailbroken due to a hardware issue that Nintendo couldn’t patch out. These exploits didn’t appear to hinder the consoles’ successes, but Nintendo remains resolute in its fury against such actions.

By October 26, hackers had figured out how to get more out of the Switch 2’s very limited exploit, able to dump games as ROMs and dig into the console’s file systems, which would usually be the beginning of emulation plans and homebrew development. Now, however, as reported by Oatmeal Dome, all this is patched out by the device’s 23.5.0 firmware update.

The OS exploit used in the recent jailbreak has been patched in version 23.5.0.

Dumping and modding games will be impossible again from this point forward, with the exception of some cartridge games (and maybe game updates) that are released in the near future.

— OatmealDome (@OatmealDome) November 10, 2026

This is possible because the issues discovered were software based, rather than something intrinsic to the physical hardware inside the Switch 2, as had been the case for the original model of the Switch 1. There, Nintendo had to change the manufacturing, and there was little that could be done to stop Switch 1 users from taking advantage, so long as they didn’t log in to Nintendo’s online services. Of course, of the tens of millions of people who owned the Switch that could do it, vanishingly few actually did, and software sales broke all of Nintendo’s records.

Eventually the crackers will find a way, because eventually they always do, but in this case it could be many years away.

I really wasn't expecting Microsoft Paint to turn up in the cybersecurity headlines, but here we are. MS disclosed and patched a security vulnerability within the software on October 13, but it's worth checking your own Paint version to see if you've received the update.

Some users don't have automatic Microsoft Store updates enabled, especially those on work machines. As Paint is updated via the store, you may need to manually update to version 11.2609.401.0 to keep your machine secure.

To confuse things further, International Cyber Digest reports that the MS store was providing older versions to some users until recently, and Windows Latest didn't seem to receive the new version even with auto updates enabled. Or, there's been some mixup with release numbers. It's genuinely difficult to tell at this point, with differing information coming from multiple sources.

The vulnerability was initially given an 8.1 severity rating on the CVSS scale, but Microsoft downgraded it to a 7.0 score on November 9 according to Threat Defence. MS also changed its description of the bug to that of a local exploit (requiring a user to open a crafted file) rather than a network attack vector, .

Regardless, to check whether your Paint version is hopefully up-to-date (what a world we live in), open the app, go to the Settings menu, and check the version number beneath the "About Paint" section. If it's lower than version 11.2609.401.0, open the Microsoft Store and manually update the app. Or, if your Windows 11 settings don't allow user updates, contact your sysadmin.

You can also check your Paint version within Windows Powershell by running:

Honestly, this is the biggest omnishambles of conflicting cybersecurity info I've seen in a while. Some outlets initially reported the bug as a no-click security flaw, while others have suggested that the vulnerability could potentially be exploited via a specially crafted image. Microsoft shifting the security goalposts as it goes really hasn't helped, nor has its apparently messy roll out of the patched version.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Anyway, it's still worth checking if Paint has been updated, folks. One way or another, we'll get to the bottom of this eventually. Or we'll just keep updating every aspect of our machines on a tediously regular basis, in the hope that some of these messy leak-plugging antics might do some good.

#3758. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation after admitting affair with alleged Chinese spy in company-wide email

"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into its own CEO Jensen Huang, after a report by the New York Times claimed he had been participating in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang admitted to having an affair in a company-wide statement, apologising to his wife as well as to Nvidia employees. Following this acknowledgement, independent investigators are looking into whether or not he's been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Per the New York Times article, the alleged spy was named as Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. Jensen Huang wrote in his internal letter: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

With regard to security concerns surrounding the CEO of US-based company Nvidia potentially sharing information with a spy, Huang confirmed that the Nvidia board of directors had initiated an investigation. He added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." The Nvidia board has said it has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Huang will remain CEO of Nvidia while the investigation is conducted. The New York Times report also claimed that US government officials did not believe Huang knew of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

Following the internal letter from Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock took a tumble from $162bn to $150bn. Nvidia, a juggernaut in the video game hardware industry, is also a key player in the global generative AI industry, which is currently carrying the US economy as other sectors struggle. The company is responsible for AI technology like DLSS 5, which generates lighting, shadows and more using generative AI.

Concerns around the Chinese AI sector passing the American industry has been a core argument against AI development slowdown or regulation, and it's also why Huang's affair may be a matter of national interest.

As of late, 90 Day Fiancé's Sarper Güven has been dipping his toes into the world of stand-up comedy. That venture is apparently proving to be fruitful as well, as he's allegedly making bank, if these latest court filings are to be believed. As Sarper and Shekinah continue to navigate the divorce process following their time on The Last Resort, it's being alleged that he has cleared over six figures from touring over the past year.

The latest news comes from TMZ, which reports that Shekinah is seeking thousands in monthly spousal support. It's a steep sum, even with both coming off the 2026 TV schedule where they netted pay for appearances within the TLC franchise. If these numbers are accurate, however, I'm shocked to say it might be justified.

Per a post on TMZ's Threads account, Shekinah wants $6,189 a month in spousal support, as well as reimbursement for $35,000 in legal fees. She went on to claim in court documents that Sarper's stand-up comedy netted $280,000 on their joint tax returns, with a $180,000 net profit.

I find that number more jaw-dropping than Sarper's body count. Sure, I'd previously written about him selling out comedy shows, but 90 Day Fiancé fans have witnessed a lot of his comedy already. I personally hadn't seen anything on TV that convinced me his stand-up was worth the price of admission, but it would seem some people do!

Shekinah also alleged in the court documents that her own business suffered a net loss of $55,000 due to her closing down the business temporarily to support Sarper on tour. The only thing I can think of is how ironic it is that Sarper might not be on the line for any of this had he signed the prenuptial agreement like she originally requested.

While none have ever presented a full pay stub to see, the general consensus amongst 90 Day stars is that they don't make a ton of money doing the show. To that point, Stephanie Matto alleged she only made a couple thousand dollars per episode. Also, while it's true that not all cast members are paid the same, many of them keep their day jobs in addition to doing the show.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way Just Hit On Andi And Nigel's Biggest Issue, And I Don't See Them Getting Over It

All this to say, while some reality shows allow their stars enough money that they can live off that alone, that doesn't seem to be the case for 90 Day stars. That makes it even wilder that Sarper has reportedly made so much money from his stand-up comedy work alone, especially when he's playing relatively small venues.

As these divorce proceedings continue, it'll be interesting to see what information may come out as a result. Shekinah and Sarper were on 90 Day Fiancé for many seasons, and I'd be curious to see what, if anything, comes out about the show as they make filings.

Neither of the two is currently on 90 Day Fiancé, but Sarper is rumored to be returning in a future season of The Single Life. As for Shekinah, she's allegedly done appearing on TLC, but we'll see if she follows through on that promise.

#3755. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

I'll be the first to admit I've said some incredibly questionable-sounding things while playing videogames. Or talking about them in public. But I would like to think that the one place where I would be extra careful about the words coming out of my mouth are in an airport, or on an airplane. Really, anywhere with an insane amount of security and an ever-pervasive fear of anything explosives-related.

Unfortunately, for passengers on board a Frontier Airlines flight earlier this week, however, one such gamer was not so cautious. As reported by CBS News, one plane at California's Ontario International Airport had to be evacuated over a bomb scare, only for it to be some guy playing Call of Duty with his pal.

According to reports, one passenger overheard words such as "bomb" and "explosion" and, rightly so, went and told staff about it. The situation led to both the plane and the east wing of Terminal 2 being evacuated, and a check of the aircraft which revealed that no explosives or bombs were on board.

After detaining and speaking to the culprit, it was revealed that he was, in fact, on FaceTime with his buddy while playing Call of Duty together. He was released without any charges, and the flight was reboarded and departed later that night.

I do feel a little bad for laughing about it—as a nervous flyer, I know for a fact that if I had been that passenger overhearing the conversation I may very well have gone into full-blown panic mode. I don't even like when someone doesn't put their phone on airplane mode as we're taking off!

But I'm also the type of person to watch my friend's Discord streams while I'm out and about, and I honestly dread to think about the kind of things passerbys have heard me say while spectating games. Hell, I'm sure even my neighbours have heard some absurd sentences leave my mouth when I've been raiding in Final Fantasy 14 with the windows wide open. If you're reading this neighbours, I'm sorry.

#3752. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

#3751. Report: James Gunn Ousted Amid Messy Power Struggle Despite Superman’s Success

ClayfaceDC StudiosJames GunnPeter SafranSupergirlSuperman

Yesterday, James Gunn and Peter Safran stepped down from their positions as co-presidents at DC Studios. This was after just four years on the job and only three movies in the new superhero cinematic universe they were overseeing. The pair has now been replaced by ex-Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham, whose evangelical history has given some DC fans pause. So what happened? According to a new report by The Hollywood Reporter, trouble had been brewing for the pair as soon as the Skydance merger went through earlier this year.

According to THR‘s sources, on Friday, November 6, Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz informed the pair that, despite previously being told they would be part of the company moving forward, there had been a “change of plans.” The shake-up had reportedly been in the works since “early fall,” with Latcham having been contacted about potentially taking over DC Studios by Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chair John Greenstein, who worked with Latcham during his time at Marvel.

THR says that there were multiple points of “tension” between Gunn and Safran on one hand and the Skydance execs on the other. Gunn and Safran initially reported directly to Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav, and their contracts said they would maintain that kind of direct reporting structure even in the event of a change in leadership, so they would have reported to Ellison following the merger. Meanwhile, Greenstein and co-chair Dana Goldberg were reportedly trying to consolidate movie production under their leadership, while Gunn and Safran had grown “accustomed to having strong control” over anything under the DC Studios banner.

Other points of contention included that Gunn and Safran were reportedly âslowâ and “not forthcoming” in sharing plans and footage with the Skydance leads.

Many will point to Supergirl‘s box office bomb as a sticking point, and I’ve even seen a lot of people joke that Gunn and Safran only got “one bad movie” before they were thrown out. While Supergirl‘s performance is noted as a problem by THR‘s sources, apparently even their biggest hit, Superman, wasn’t doing enough in the eyes of their corporate overlords. That film, which grossed $618 million on a $225 budget, “did not net out, or have the kind of pop culture impact, in the way that kind of movie should,” in the eyes of Skydance.

Sources say that Gunn is “somewhat relieved” to be out of the business side of things and now focusing on filmmaking. His DC next film, Man of Tomorrow, is set to premiere next year.

As for Latcham, THR‘s sources call him a “down-the-middle shooter” who is more concerned with making “hits for the masses” than Gunn, whose projects often feature somewhat profane writing and obscure characters.

Clayface, the last DC Studios project produced while Gunn and Safran were company co-presidents, is in theaters now.

#3750. How to change layers in WoW Forever? (After the layer size change)

If you want to play with friends in WoW: Forever, you have to go back to one of WoW's most dreaded concepts - layers and shards.

World of Warcraft: Forever skips realms and introduces gameplay rulesets instead, where you can pick your preferred playstyle and get whisked to an Azeroth populated with like-minded individuals. But things can get complicated if, say, you want to play with your friends or guildmates from across the world.

Plus, it’s not like Blizzard will squeeze everyone using your gameplay ruleset into the same world instance. This is where layers come in, and it’s similar to, but also very different from, its original iteration in Classic.

Others new to WoW might be wondering what exactly layers are, and how they might affect their WoW: Forever experience.

So we know MMOs have servers, and each WoW server has a realm that contains a version of Azeroth and the players inside it. Of course, we can’t expect Blizzard to spawn everyone at once, since we’d overcrowd the game world and break the experience.

When a location gets a high-enough population, WoW uses sharding to copy the area into a “shard” and transfers some players there. A shard is a perfectly working copy of a location, complete with NPCs and objects, except you can only see and interact with players of the same shard.

The idea is to manage overpopulation by keeping player counts at a certain number. This keeps lag manageable and ensures there are enough mobs and quest items for everyone in any given zone.

Since shards are zone-wide, you can see players “disappear” into a new zone because they’re crossing over to a new shard (called phasing). If you’re approaching a zone where all shards are at capacity, you’d hit a soft “loading” queue before you enter. Worst case, you get disconnected from the server, which can ruin your momentum.

WoW Retail still uses sharding. It sometimes implements cross-realm zones (CRZs), so low-population realms can share low-population zones.

We got to layering at the launch of WoW Classic in 2019, where it was presented as a bigger solution to server population. Sharding at the time just didn’t feel like a practical choice, as they’d have to create hundreds of shards per zone.

“We had some serious concerns about what would happen when realms started to mature, and populations shifted,” Blizzard noted about sharding in the release of Battle for Wintergrasp in Wrath Classic. “Would we have hundreds of realms with low populations a few months in?”

So they came up with layers, which is sharding but applied to the whole game world. Upon meeting specific population conditions, Blizzard can create a copy of Azeroth and transfer players there.

But it’s not a perfect solution. Too much layering could result in dead cities, and too little overcrowds areas. It can hurt the economy as well, as you can layer-hop to get more resources from another layer once your layer’s route runs out.

Classic moved away from layering just a few months in November 2019 and converged everyone into a single layer.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Players reintroduced the layering and sharding discourse back into Forever overpopulation concerns during launch. We don’t have the full picture of how Blizzard is managing Forever servers as of writing, but players seem to have noticed enough to make informed assumptions:

Instead of realms, we choose a ruleset that represents our preferred playstyle and play with others who choose the same. In theory, it’s a “realmless” system, and our ruleset of choice is functionally a mega server that our fellow ruleset comrades share.

Forever seems to have retained the Retail sharding system. But this time, there’s a chance you can auto-switch layers during the transition. This seems to have carried over from beta. Redditor u/Kellian noted that per-zone “loading” means hostiles and friendlies phase in and out, and can even stop PvP.

Building upon the ruleset is what Blizzard called the familiar faces system. As explained in their BlizzCon 2026 deep-dive, this will have players more consistently encounter the same strangers throughout their leveling journey. The goal is for these familiar faces to give Forever a stronger sense of community spirit, and may even encourage teaming up while you level. This also extends to guilds, so they can potentially pull you into their layers.

At random intervals during your sessions (sometimes none at all), you might encounter a prompt that warns you of a World Refresh. Either you do the refresh now or wait a couple of minutes. This isn’t any cause for alarm, as it just means the game will transfer you to a new instance or layer.

These refreshes often happen to balance the current population. You remain in the same spot, but your immediate surroundings might be different, like there might be more players, more mobs, or both.

Switching between layers in Forever can be done in a variety of ways, but there’s no manual options button to do so. Instead, you can do some things to “force” your way into a layer switch. Popular methods you can try include:

At launch, game dev Aggrend said they would look into how players lamented how sparsely populated the game world felt. A few days later, some players noticed so many characters for so few mobs.

This was especially challenging in PvP, where one faction can dominate a layer and make it difficult for the opposing one to level up or gather resources.

Redditor u/sknilegap doesn’t even call it layering at all, but actually just sharding. And their problem has less to do with the technology itself, but more with its impact on the experience at large.

“I am fine with the necessity of the system. Just keep it immersive,” they said in their post. “Make me sticky to those crossing over around the same time window as me. So […] we all see each other on the other side of the next zone, grouped or not.”

You can play World of Warcraft: Forever on PC and macOS.

Johnny Depp was wrapped up in legal issues and personal matters during the early 2020s, with the biggest situation being his defamation case with former wife Amber Heard. The Oscar nominee received a mostly favorable verdict in 2022 and, since then, he’s been easing his way back into the entertainment industry. On that note, his latest feature is the 2026 movie schedule entry, Ebenezer. Now, amid this phase of his career, one of Depp’s most recent producers is getting real about the prospect of his comeback.

In 2023, Depp starred in the French historical drama film Jeanne du Barry, and the film sees him play the role of Louis XV. Nellee Holmes served as one of the executive producers on that film, and she recently spoke to CNN as part of a wide ranging story on Depp. Holmes was quite complimentary of the actor, calling him a “good human being.” In the producer’s estimation, Depp has forged connections with “people who trust him” and still believe in him. As for the quality of the leading man’s work, Holmes had this to say:

You cannot say anything that makes him bad. His work is his weapon.

In terms of Jeanne du Barry, the film generated headlines several years back due to being Depp’s first post-trial movie. The biopic was directed by Maïwenn, who also co-starred alongside Depp as the titular character. Ultimately, the movie debuted at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2023, and Depp received a standing ovation. Despite that praise, Maïwenn would later claim Depp was “difficult” to work with due to creative differences and personal conduct.

All that aside, though, Holmes is of the belief that Ebenezer will mark a turning point for Depp. The film was announced back in October 2025 and, at that time, it was also confirmed that horror maven Ti West would direct it. Months ago, West praised Depp’s portrayal of the titular Ebenezer Scrooge, noting that he possesses that “cadence and that musicality to the way that he performs.”. Another bit of praise came from Depp’s co-star, Rupert Grint, who simply referred to him as “so iconic.”

This holiday flick isn’t the only production Depp has on the horizon either. He’s also set to headline Day Drinker, which is a supernatural thriller film from director Marc Webb that’s set to be released amid the 2027 movie schedule. There have also been rumblings regarding a third Pirates of the Caribbean film being in the works, thanks to comments from producer Jerry Bruckheimer. It’s unknown if Depp would star in the film, but he joked about possibly not being able to grow facial hair again should he reprise Captain Jack Sparrow.

Ironically, amid talk about Depp making a “comeback” in Hollywood, he prefers not to use that term. Depp previously admitted to being confused by the word being applied to his circumstances, because he “didn’t go anywhere” to begin with. Still, it does indeed seem that the star’s career is on an upward trajectory and, all the while, he seems to have people like Nelle Holmes and Ti West in his corner.

Check out Johnny Depp in Ebenezer when it opens in theaters on November 13. Also, be on the lookout for Day Drinker, which is set to hit cinemas on March 26, 2027.

#3748. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

It goes without saying (yet here I am saying it) that Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be huge. We don't really have a sense as to just how huge at this point: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has boasted that GTA 6 preorder numbers are "unprecedented," but he's refused to provide specifics because "the raw numbers could be potentially misleading." "Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony proclaimed on the PlayStation Blog. That's roughly double what Take-Two took in during the same quarter in its previous year, when it reported net bookings of $1.76 billion.

"The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is ten days away and, with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels, we expect to deliver an historic year for our company," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said during yesterday's quarterly financial report.

#3746. Rockstar Says GTA 6 Is ‘Targeting’ 30 FPS And Will Use PSSR On PS5 Pro

If you pre-ordered a digital version of GTA VI, you can preload it right now, and considering its massive file-size, getting a nine-day head start on that download might be a good idea. But in addition to announcing the pre-load, Rockstar Games has revealed some extra information on the game’s specifications and features, and a brief but glittery new trailer to accompany the announcement.

The biggest thing on the list of specifications is the framerate. Sorry to anyone hoping for a buttery-smooth 60 FPS on console but GTA VI, according to Rockstar, is “targeting 30 frames per second.” That word “targeting” seems especially fraught, suggesting you might not even get all 30 frames all the time.

On the PS5 Pro the game will make use of PSSR upscaling and feature ray-tracing while your regular degular PS5 consoles get “high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering […], and improved load times.”

Over on the Xbox side of things, you’ll be able to play the game via Xbox Cloud Streaming on the X and S console, and on the Xbox One with Series S graphics. Rockstar warns that trying to stream the game might lead to some technical difficulties. “Connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay,” Rockstar’s announcement reads. “GTAVI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.”

It is not long now, and with this new information, GTA VI feels even closer.

#3744. "Something's really possible" - Mass Effect cast rally around efforts to save the franchise on the first N7 Day after BioWare's closure

I'm Commander Shepard and this is my favorite video on the internet.

This N7 Day was the first without developer BioWare around, but fans of the Mass Effect series didn't let 7th November go by quietly. The community managed to get several notable Mass Effect actors to lend their voice to the increasingly loud 'SaveMassEffect' movement.

In the weeks since BioWare's shock closure and Mass Effect Universe's cancellation, the community-organised We Are Mass Effect group have put up billboards in Times Square, a mobile billboard outside BioWare Edmonton's former office and much more while directing attention to an online petition.

Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI

And for the series' annual celebration, the group managed to get a sizable portion of the Mass Effect cast to join in. Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, original trilogy composer Sam Hulick, Garrus' Brandon Keener, Jack's Courtnay Taylor, Tali'Zorah's Ash Sroka, Thane's Keythe Farley and many more all showed up in a two-minute video to help potentially salvage the series - sometimes in character.

"When we heard about the formal closing of Boware, I felt weirdly hopeful," Hale said in a separate interview with IGN. "I can't explain it. I just got so weirdly hopeful. My first thought, of course, was for the devs and all the people. And then I just closed my eyes and crossed my fingers and I said, 'I feel something's possible. You know, something's really possible.'"

The other half of Commander Shepard, Mark Meer, noted that "this didn't all just happen in the last 10 days." Near yearly layoffs at EA had slowly trimmed multiple BioWare teams down, sometimes even affecting studio veterans who had been at the company for decades.

"A lot of senior writers within the last year or two were let go. People who had been there from the very beginning. Again, people who had built that company from the ground up, who built the bones of it, who made those games that had captured people so much right back from the 1990s," Meer said.

Henry Cavill is never afraid to get his geek on, and I love that for him. More importantly, he’s not afraid to do so while raising awareness for an important cause. All this month, the Movember Foundation is raising money for and shining a light on important topics in men’s health, from cancer awareness to mental health support. So naturally, this means Cavill is back with a mustache for Movember (and totally pulls it off).

The Superman actor is a long time supporter of the foundation, having previously grown a mustache in support. This time, the actor is embracing his nerdy side as his latest team up pairs him with Google’s Antigravity (an AI tool on Googlebook) to create a 16-bit game called “Mustache Protocol.” In it, a suspiciously Cavill-looking mustachioed hero is making his mission to stop rogue CGI artists from erasing all the mustaches in the world. The actor post Part 2 (of a three part series) on his Instagram:

A post shared by Henry Cavill (@henrycavill)

As you can see, the hero has lots of muscles and a handlebar mustache very similar to the Witcher actor’s own fancy ‘stache. While the attention should be primarily on raising awareness for Movemeber, it’s hard to miss the cheeky humor presented in the video, specifically the arm re-load. Now, you maybe thinking, "huh, that looks a little familiar." Well, you’d be right. This is a fun nod to Cavill’s role in Mission Impossible - Fallout, which fans helpfully dropped in the comments in the form of gifs. You know, in case you needed reminding.

Paramount has previously used the mustache in that movie when the studio made a donation to the Movember Foundation. However, that’s not what Cavill is winking at in the video. He dropped an “IYKYK” when giving his hero a “little pocket,” which if you know, is another Mission Impossible reference. If you don’t, this is slightly poking fun at continuity errors in the movie, which yes, included disappearing pockets, but fans are here for the 'stache:

The actor is clearly having fun taking a break from several projects, including a Highlander reboot movie, and doing so for a worthy cause. Though I wasn’t surprised to see the style of the game had a delightful vintage feel to it. The stylistic choices really show off Cavill’s personality, and that’s why fans are loving the videos. Only he could make brisket feel like a reasonable health choice for a power up. Part of the joy in watching the actor create something so wholesome is seeing him show off his wonderfully geeky side, which fans get to see often. Surely the “game of the year awards” is Cavill’s for the taking, right?

Whether it’s his love of the Witcher video games or working with Amazon on the Warhammer 40,000 series, he’s never strayed from being just like the rest of us. He’s also reportedly attached to the Voltron live action adaptation of the animated series from the ‘80s. Though I have no information on whether or not he'll have a fancy 'stache.

I mustache you to remember that while you're supporting all of these projects, that you also check out the foundation's website and note the importance of the 'stache this Movember.

#3742. GTA 6 pre-orders are tracking "well above expectations" and the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two, says CEO Strauss Zelnick

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick noted that pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking "far above expectations", and is certain that soon "numbers will speak for themselves" when it comes to the game.

Zelnick also promised GTA Online and GTA 5 will continue to receive updates in order to support the "nearly 235 million" units sold to date across "an unprecedented three console generations". The GTA series as a whole has, to date, sold over 480 million units. Karl Statoff, president at Take-Two, adds the launch of GTA 6 will be a "defining moment for the company and global entertainment industry". Zelnick adds, later in a question and answer session, that he expects GTA 6 to "set a new baseline" for Take-Two. "The future's really bright across the board," he notes.

For the next quarter, Take-Two expects to deliver $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion - with "recurrent consumer spending" to raise by 12 percent, driven by "the groundbreaking release" of Grand Theft Auto 6, and expects to see "significant growth for the Grand Theft Auto series", driven by sales of - specifically - Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content, and that most people are pre-ordering at its $100 price point. That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

Bring Up The Bodies, often regarded as Hilary Mantel's masterpiece (more of a Place Of Greater Safety man myself), opens thus: "His children are falling from the sky. He watches from horse-back, acres of England stretching behind him; they drop, gilt-winged, each with a blood-filled gaze".

This is a description of Thomas Cromwell's falcons in 1535. It is also a description of the life of Franklin Clinton in 2026. Los Santos is awash in bodies because I have installed PeopleFalling – BloodSky, a mod which sends an endless wave of people plummeting to Earth like a horrible hard rain. "A modification called 'People Falling' or as I call it, 'Blood Sky'", writes the author, confusingly, as they presumably chose both names.

"When you press the 'X' key, characters drop from the sky. You can change the activation button in the .ini file". This is a lie. It's actually the B key. My relationship with PeopleFalling AKA BloodSky got off to a rocky start.

It does work though. Sort of. Tap B (not X) and the rainy season begins—people fall silently to the ground in a kind of reverse-Rapture situation, absolutely all of them physics-free and adopting the same stomach-sleeper position when they finally make contact with sidewalk, with highway, with rooftop.

Then it ends, and no matter how much you tap B—notifications reading "Falling people Active" and "Falling People Deactive" flashing in the lower right of your screen—they never come back. It's like you have witnessed a beautiful, once-in-a-lifetime miracle, like a full solar eclipse or Halley's comet.

Also, when the process is ongoing it really alarms my bodyguard, who responds like a dog hearing a bang in the house at night.

#3739. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Has A Massive Second-Act Change That Took My Breath Away

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Last night in my playthrough of Ocarina of Time, I finished up the Fire Temple and headed (as one does) to Zora Domain, expecting it to be (as the rest of the game has been so far) very much like the original in structure, just visually more elaborate. And it was, mostly. But as I passed through the realm, I also encountered one of my favorite new additions to the remake so far, one that simultaneously clears up one of Ocarina of Time‘s long-enduring inconsistencies, while also adding pretty significant elements of both horror and hope to the original story.

In the original Ocarina of Time, Zora Domain in the adult timeline is completely frozen over. When Link enters, there are no Zora to be foundâjust an iced-over pond and a frozen waterfall. At the top, you can find King Zora, encased in red ice. Through your adventures in Ice Cavern and later Water Temple, you learn that Ganondorf is (of course) responsible, and that all the Zora have been completely frozen. Sheik was able to save Ruto, who goes on to become the Sage of Water, and you’re later able to thaw out King Zora using Blue Fire.

But the fate of the rest of the Zora is sort of…ambiguous. Presumably due to technical limitations in the original, Zora Domain in adult timeline remains frozen over even post-Water Temple, and the Zora people are nowhere to be found. It’s just King Zora, sitting on his icy throne, for the rest of the game, and Ruto now effectively dead to the world in the Sacred Realm as a sage. You do see some Zora in the credits sequence at the end of the game, implying that some survived, but just what happened to Hyrule’s aquatic folk more broadly remains pretty murky.

The remake clears that up, but the way it does this made me say “holy shit”Â out loud several times.

When you enter Zora Domain as adult Link, you’re treated to a souped-up version of the same sight: frozen pond, frozen waterfall, frozen everything. New to the remake is a haunting new piece of music that does a great job of conveying the frozen emptiness you’re faced with. I hate that you can occasionally hear snippets of the main Zora theme instruments creeping in between the weird, spooky noises! Agh!

But even worse (read: better) than this is what you see when you go out onto the pond. And look down. Into the ice.

Uh, yeah. That’s what that is. That’s where they are. They are actively frozen beneath their own pond. You can just. See them. Down there. Trapped. Dead? Effectively tortured by cold?! Holy shit.

I haven’t finished the Water Temple yet. I considered waiting until I had finished it to write this blog, but I decided to write it now because I wanted to talk about the other emotion, aside from horror, that seeing this inspired. If the Zora are in there now, that opens the door for them to be freed when I finish Water Temple. There are no technical limitations prohibiting Nintendo from thawing out Zora Domain when the time comes and giving these people their lives back. Can Ruto and I really, truly, conclusively save the Zora this time around?

Right now, I am loving the anticipation! I can’t wait to finish the Water Temple tonight, and while I’m a little afraid of being disappointed by the outcome in case Nintendo decided to leave the Zora in this horrible frozen state until the credits, the overall excellence and attention to detail of the Ocarina of Time remake so far has given me ample reason for hope.

#3738. As investors ask about GTA 6 and AI, Take-Two CEO once again puts faith in dev creativity, states making hit games "remains the purview of human beings"

"Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future."

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick fielded questions from investors after presenting the financial results of the company. One caller was concerned about AI - specifically about the proliferation of AI-powered compilations and decompilations that have been raising piracy concerns for publishers over the past few weeks.

Zelnick notes that "[the video games] business has been largely immune to piracy" thanks to factors like file size, how console ecosystems work, and aspects related to the online nature of the games industry. That said, Strauss continues, there is a threat posed to the industry because of AI. However, he assures listening investors that Take-Two is appropriately scaling its measures against bad faith actors using artificial intelligence.

"We are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And - at the same time, without in any way being cavalier - every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy, [and] this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Zelnick pivots back to AI again later in the call, where one investor once again asks about AI, seemingly keen to learn whether the CEO feels it can provide GTA 6 developer Rockstar with any kind of "competitive advantage" in the games industry. Given Zelnick's previous comments on the subject, his answer was not a complete surprise.

"It's always been true [that technology benefits us]," explains Zelnick. "We've always created our entertainment inside computers with technology. All advances have benefited us, and I don't expect that that will change - in fact, I hope it'll accelerate. I think at the same time, what we're known for [at Take-Two] is the desire to make the best entertainment on Earth. And, more often than not, we have succeeded - and the creativity that drives that success is human creativity harnessing technology. And I think that's what you'll see in the future, too.

"Undoubtedly some of the most recent technological advances that you've seen have made it easier to create assets. Where all that is consistent with the story of our business. When I started in interactive entertainment (longer ago than I would like to say), it was really difficult to create an asset in a computer. Today, it's a whole lot easier - but you know what's not easier? Making a big hit. Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future. And hit creation remains the purview of human beings."

This isn't the first instance of AI skepticism we've seen from Strauss Zelnick. Back in March, he outright rejected the idea that AI can tackle games on the scale of GTA 6. Elsewhere in the call, the Take-Two CEO reiterated how well GTA 6 is tracking as he reasserted pre-order numbers are well above expectations, and promised that the success of the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two's gaming business.
